nodes.label: Indictments and Charge Sheets
nodes.summary: Drafting charges, filing/service, amendment, joinder/severance, quashing, and plea.

nodes.label: Drafting Charge / Indictment
nodes.summary: Particulars: must give reasonable information as to the nature of the offence; include date, place, person, property, statutory provision. Duplicity: one offence per count (no duplicity). Uncertainty: charge must be sufficiently clear; otherwise subject to motion to quash.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Leung Kwok Hung (1996)
nodes.summary: Indictment quashed for defect/duplicity.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Tam Shing Hoi (2004)
nodes.summary: Indictment defect and uncertainty.

nodes.label: Filing and Service
nodes.summary: Charge sheet filed in magistracy; indictment filed in CFI after committal. Service on accused; indictment must be signed by law officer.

nodes.label: Amendment of Indictment
nodes.summary: Court may amend indictment at any stage before verdict if no injustice (Cap 221 s.23). If amendment raises new issues, adjournment may be needed.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.23
nodes.summary: Court may amend indictment at any stage before verdict if no injustice.

nodes.label: Joinder and Severance
nodes.summary: Joinder of counts: may join multiple charges if founded on same facts or form part of a series of similar character (Cap 221 s.16). Joinder of defendants: may be tried jointly if alleged to have committed same offence or connected offences (s.17). Severance: court may order separate trials if joinder prejudicial or embarrassing (s.18).

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.16
nodes.summary: Joinder of counts: same facts or series of similar character.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.17
nodes.summary: Joinder of defendants: same or connected offences.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.18
nodes.summary: Severance: court may order separate trials if joinder prejudicial or embarrassing.

nodes.label: Talbot v R (PC) (comparative)
nodes.summary: Severance test; prejudice not curable by jury direction.

nodes.label: Quashing Indictment
nodes.summary: Application to quash for formal defect or abuse of process. Must show substantial prejudice; court will amend rather than quash if possible.

nodes.label: Plea
nodes.summary: Arraignment in CFI/DC; plea to each count. Guilty plea: court must ensure plea is unequivocal and voluntary; factual basis agreed or resolved by Newton hearing. Alternative offences: jury may convict of lesser alternative if supported by evidence.

nodes.label: Criminal Procedure Ordinance (Cap 221) s.51
nodes.summary: Alternative offences: jury may convict of lesser alternative if supported by evidence.

nodes.label: R v Tailford (comparative)
nodes.summary: Plea to alternative offence not averred in indictment.

nodes.label: HKSAR v Asif Ahfaq Mehmood
nodes.summary: Alternative offence issue under Cap 221 s.51.

nodes.label: Indictment Flow: Proceedings Instituted
nodes.summary: Step 1: Criminal proceedings are instituted by information, complaint, or charge sheet.

nodes.label: Indictment Flow: Offence Classification
nodes.summary: Step 2: Classify the offence as summary, indictable, or either way.

nodes.label: Indictment Flow: Indictment Drafted
nodes.summary: Step 3: Draft indictment with proper particulars, avoiding duplicity.

nodes.label: Indictment Flow: Particulars Checked
nodes.summary: Step 4: Check particulars for date, place, person, property, and statutory provision.

nodes.label: Indictment Flow: Filing and Service
nodes.summary: Step 5: File indictment and serve on accused.

nodes.label: Indictment Flow: Amendment/Severance/Joinder
nodes.summary: Step 6: Consider amendment, severance, or joinder issues.

nodes.label: Indictment Flow: Plea
nodes.summary: Step 7: Arraignment and plea to each count.

nodes.label: Indictment Flow: Trial or Disposal
nodes.summary: Step 8: Proceed to trial or other disposal (guilty plea, discharge, etc.).
